reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 18 and fresh: SPX closed 7,323.63, down 6.64% from its 120-day high of 7,844.52, 4.25% below its 50-day and 0.31% below its 200-day (7,346.55). SMH ($459.54) and NVDA ($150.96) are both BELOW Zone 2, VIX is 24.56 with no rollover, HY OAS is 3.43 and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4 (credit only).
reaction.invalidation: SPX closes back above the 7,750-7,820 failure zone with SMH reclaiming $580 and VIX under 20 — the correction thesis is void and the stance flips to Add. Conversely, HY OAS above 4% with SPX below 7,000 voids the rotation read and the episode becomes a rollover, not a correction.

ladder.response: Stand down on all new AI deployment; no Tranche A. Wait for a failed first bounce plus a second low that holds before re-testing any buy zone.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $440 or SPX closes below 7,020 (next zone down)

ladder.response: Do not chase the bounce. Treat the failure zone as the trap case: no new entries on the rally, and re-test verdict decides whether the correction resumes or voids.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone: SMH rallies into $580-600 or SPX into 7,750-7,820 and fails there

ladder.response: Full stand-down per the ladder: no new deployment of any tranche; review speculative holdings (CONL, BMNR) for trim candidates.
ladder.trigger: Stand-down / regime break: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25 while SPX holds below its 200-day

ladder.response: Tranche A re-arms: 25% deployment per the ladder, sized to the name that reclaimed its zone, with the failure-zone retest as the invalidation.
ladder.trigger: Re-entry: SMH or NVDA closes back inside Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 or more of 4

reaction.trapRisk: Today's bounce is the trap setup in miniature: QQQ +2.34% and TQQQ +7.06% while NVDA is down 1.69% on the day and both SMH and NVDA remain below Zone 2. A pivot-and-fail here means the first bounce suckers in buyers before the failure-zone retest. Entries change accordingly: no chasing the first bounce, no sizing on intraday strength — only a Zone 2 reclaim on a close, with the tally rising, authorizes the first probe.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is active but unconfirmed as a bottom: both SMH and NVDA sit below their Zone 2 floors, the mechanical tally is 1 of 4, and the overnight bounce (QQQ +2.34%, TQQQ +7.06%) is led by breadth while NVDA itself is down 1.69% on the day — no Tranche A condition is met.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, not dismissing: the index is being held up by names outside the AI complex while the names that dominate it by weight fall. If credit flips — HY OAS above 4% — the rotation read dies and the rollover read takes over. Until then, the damage is concentrated, not systemic.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER. Mag 7 names sit on average 18.74% below their 52-week highs against SPY only 6.6% below its high — a 12.14-point divergence gap — with NVDA weakest at -38% and AAPL strongest at -2.3%. Credit does not confirm a rollover: HY OAS is 3.43 and calm, and bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold. SPX itself is only 6.64% off its 120-day high (7,844.52) at the Nov 18 close of 7,323.63.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: Headlines read as an AI bust: the Nov 18 FOMC minutes show almost every Fed official discussing the risk of an AI bust, and the Mag 7 complex is down hard. The tape is being read as the start of a broad rollover.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4% while SPX holds below its 200-day (7,346.55) would void the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Oversold plus growing revenue is the setup, not the trigger. The mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4 — credit calm is the sole confirmed signal; there is no zone occupancy, no volume climax reversal, and no VIX rollover (VIX 24.56, 5-day high 25.46). Buying into the fall without a Zone 2 reclaim is catching a knife the ladder does not authorize.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data has not broken. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits 38% below its high; AVGO revenue is up 55% while 28.5% below its high; Datadog revenue is up 27.7% with an 80% gross margin and a 29.2% free-cash-flow margin while 44.4% below its high; MU sits 43.8% below its high at $705.27 with RSI 37. Of the 35 tracked dislocations, the dominant decline reason is SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not a fundamental break. Both SMH ($459.54) and NVDA ($150.96) sit below their Zone 2 floors ($470-505 and $175-185), so the tape has overshot the ladder's buy zones to the downside.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market has priced the AI buildout as a circular-finance bust: SMH is down 31.6% from its high and NVDA 37.97%, with NVDA's 1-month trend at -30.3% and RSI at 21.1 — deeply oversold on a tape that treats the whole complex as impaired.
themes.watchFor: SMH or NVDA closing back inside Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 or more of 4.

themes.counterRead: Insider buying at the trough ($1.17M in VST) against an acute-catalyst decline is the classic divergence: operators buying while the tape sells. But VST's revenue inflection reads STABLE_OR_DECLINING, so the insider signal is a watch item, not a confirmed recovery — the power leg needs its own Zone 2-style reclaim before it promotes.
themes.dataAnchor: SMR is down 27.96% over one month, CCJ 21.25%, OKLO 18.27%, URA 15%. VST — a holding — sits at $125.58, 33.7% below its high, with the decline classified ACUTE_CATALYST rather than a slow fade, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. The VST watchlist promotion scores 75 with a durable-moat thesis on the nuclear-power theme. The selling is indiscriminate across the complex, not name-specific.
themes.label: AI power / nuclear unwind
themes.narrative: The power leg of the AI trade is being sold as hard as the chips: nuclear and power names are down 15-28% in a month, read as the market doubting the data-center power buildout alongside the chip buildout.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above its 50-day ($145.08) on a close, or SMR/CCJ stabilizing with a positive 5-day trend.

themes.counterRead: A 5.10% 10-year with a positive curve and calm credit (HY OAS 3.43) is a headwind for long-duration growth multiples, not a crisis. The risk is not the level — it is a further leg up in real yields while the AI complex is already below its buy zones. If the 10-year pushes sustainably higher from here, the Zone 2 floors become ceilings.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year is at 5.10% with the 2-year at 4.80%, a 2s10s curve of +0.30 — no longer inverted — and a real 10-year of 2.91% against a 3.88% policy rate. The curve has normalized, not inverted further, which is consistent with a growth scare rather than a recession call. The Dec 8-9 FOMC decision and Nov 25 PCE are the next prints; the minutes are the event, not a policy change.
themes.label: Rates and the Fed: the AI-bust debate reaches the minutes
themes.narrative: Rate-cut hopes are fading into the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision, and the Nov 18 minutes put the AI-bust risk on the Fed's own agenda — the narrative is that tight money plus a circular AI funding story ends the trade.
themes.watchFor: PCE on Nov 25 and the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision; a 10-year close sustainably above 5.5% would change the rates read.

themes.counterRead: The washout is real but concentrated in the most leveraged, most speculative names — a 58% drawdown in CONL against an 18% drawdown in Bitcoin is leverage unwinding, not a market verdict. Treating the crypto washout as a leading indicator for the broad tape over-reads it; the signal it does carry is that risk appetite in the speculative tail is gone, which usually precedes, not accompanies, a broad bottom.
themes.dataAnchor: Bitcoin is down 18.18% over one month, Ethereum 19.9%, Dogecoin 20.8%, IBIT 22.95%, Coinbase 33.27%. The leveraged end is far worse: CONL, a holding, is down 58.33% in a month. Yet SPX is only 6.64% off its high and HY OAS is 3.43 and calm — the broad market and credit do not confirm a systemic risk-off event.
themes.label: Speculative beta washout
themes.narrative: Crypto and leveraged speculative names are collapsing — read as broad risk-off and the first leg of a wider unwind.
themes.watchFor: Bitcoin stabilizing with a positive 5-day trend while CONL stops making new lows would mark the washout as exhausted rather than spreading.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds at the Zone 2 retest: SMH $470-505 and NVDA $175-185 are the trigger levels, and with NVDA revenue growing 61.4% and AVGO 55% against prices 28-38% off their highs, a Zone 2 reclaim with a rising mechanical tally is where the wave forms — not on today's bounce.
